name: mcp-http-tools v1.4.1..v1.5.0

commits.message:
feat: add --http transport with bearer-token auth

Adds a StreamableHTTPServerTransport-backed --http mode alongside the
existing stdio transport, gated by verifyBearerToken (Task 1). Serves
MCP at /mcp on 127.0.0.1:${MCP_HTTP_PORT:-3000}; requires
MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and rejects unauthenticated requests with 401.

index.js now builds a fresh Server+StreamableHTTPServerTransport pair
per HTTP request (factored into createMcpServer()) rather than reusing
one shared instance, matching the SDK's own stateless-transport
example: Server#connect() throws "Already connected to a transport" if
reused before the previous transport's close() has unset it, so a
single shared instance breaks on any request after the first.

Also fixes a pre-existing test.js bug where the "integration" describe
block's afterEach did `delete globalThis.fetch` instead of restoring
the captured realFetch reference -- since Node's global fetch is a
lazily-initialized property that doesn't come back after being deleted
once overwritten, this permanently broke the bare `fetch` global for
every describe block that runs afterward in the same process,
including the new HTTP transport tests.
feat: add verifyBearerToken helper for HTTP transport auth

name: mcp-http-tools v1.5.0..v1.6.0

commits.message:
feat: add composite tools (requests array, fan out + merge)

A tool can now declare `requests:` instead of a single `url:` -- every
request in the array runs in PARALLEL and the results merge into one JSON
object keyed by each request's `key`. Built for "give me the whole
picture" tools: a project overview pulling k8s state, logs, metrics, and
error data in one call instead of five round-trips, one per data source.

- `url`/`requests` are mutually exclusive on a tool.
- Each request entry needs a unique `key` plus its own
  url/method/headers/params/response/timeout/retry -- the exact same
  fields a regular tool uses, just nested one level down. No implicit
  param inheritance: a request only sees the args it explicitly declares.
- One request failing (timeout, non-2xx, network error) does not fail the
  others -- its key gets `{ "error": "..." }` in the merged result, so
  partial data beats an all-or-nothing failure for an overview tool.
- validateConfig's per-request validation (url/params/headers/auth/
  response/timeout/retry) is refactored into validateRequestShape(),
  shared by both a regular tool and each composite request entry --
  avoids duplicating ~180 lines of validation logic.
- callTool()'s single-request execution is renamed to callSingleRequest()
  and reused by the new callCompositeTool(), which fans out via
  Promise.allSettled and merges by key.

12 new tests, all against real local HTTP servers per this repo's
testing rule (no fetch mocking) -- including one asserting genuinely
parallel dispatch (max concurrent in-flight requests, not just total wall
time, since only checking wall time could pass on an accidental
semi-parallel implementation too).

feat: MCP_HTTP_HOST env var, defaulting to 127.0.0.1

Needed to run --http mode inside a container: a Service/reverse proxy
routes to the container's own IP, not the host's loopback, so binding
127.0.0.1 unconditionally makes the app unreachable while it logs that
it's listening. Loopback stays the default for the existing bare-host
deploy behind a local nginx.

commits.message:
Merge pull request #1 from 3h4x/fix/get-array-query-repeated-keys

fix: serialize array GET params as repeated query keys, not JSON

fix: serialize array GET params as repeated query keys, not JSON

buildRequest() was calling JSON.stringify on array-valued query params,
producing e.g. ?span_ids=["a","b"] instead of the standard repeated-key
form (?span_ids=a&span_ids=b). Frameworks like FastAPI's
Optional[list[str]] parse the former as a one-item list containing the
literal JSON string, not two items -- silently breaking any GET tool
with a type: array param against such a backend (surfaced while wiring
Arize Phoenix's REST API, which declares several Optional[list[str]]
query params, into infra's infra-mcp).

Non-array object params keep JSON-string serialization, since there's
no standard repeated-key convention for those.

chore(dependabot): per-ecosystem groups instead of multi-ecosystem-groups

Since the move to multi-ecosystem-groups on 2026-09-30, Dependabot ignored each
entry's applies-to: security-updates group and opened one PR per advisory, each
conflicting with the others' lockfile. Every entry now has its own schedule and
two groups, <eco>-minor-patch (version updates) and <eco>-security.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(dependabot): drop update-types from the minor-patch groups

A SHA-pinned action or a Docker digest bump is neither minor nor patch, so
the filter sent it to a PR of its own (seo-tools #285). Majors are already
ignored on every entry, so the filter added nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
